goals: Select a case and inspect a proof role
Use the financial worksheet and notice navigation/scroll friction

actions.action: Opened the local HTML in a fresh Chromium context, then tapped “Explore” in the header.
actions.observed: The URL fragment changed to #explorer and the browser scrolled to the case chooser at scrollY 1659. The rendered document width stayed 390px. The Explore link box measured 39×44px.
actions.taskOutcome: Reached the interactive explorer; navigation worked. The link height is 44px but its width is below 44px.
actions.evidence: Browser viewport 390×844; #explorer; Explore link bounding box x=18.72,y=72.80,w=39.05,h=44. Screenshot inputs: mobile-top.png and explorer.png.

actions.observed: The case became selected and the role list changed to Order arithmetic, Pool arithmetic, and Batch accounting. The case choice and role cards remained in the same vertical mobile flow.
actions.taskOutcome: Could change cases and see which illustrative roles belong to the selected case.
actions.evidence: Runtime aria-pressed state on the case and role buttons; role cards are approximately 60px high in the mobile layout.

actions.observed: The role card became selected and the inspector content changed to “Pool arithmetic”. The inspector begins after the diagram, explanatory copy, and three role cards; its heading was at viewport y≈718 before scrolling.
actions.taskOutcome: Role selection worked, but the selected explanation did not come into view. I had to scroll further to read it.
actions.evidence: reached-role-inspector.png shows selected Pool arithmetic and the inspector below the role list; browser bounding box for inspector heading before scroll: y=717.67.

actions.action: Scrolled to the inspector after selecting the role.
actions.observed: The inspector showed the selected role and its description, “A supported pool relation explains the pool continuation.”
actions.taskOutcome: Completed role inspection after an extra scroll.

actions.action: Tapped “Follow the value” in the header.
actions.observed: The URL fragment changed to #worksheet and the worksheet section moved to the viewport (section top y≈128).
actions.taskOutcome: The worksheet link worked; it took one long-page jump to reach the section.

actions.action: Changed the seller-payment slider from 35 to 60 CASH.
actions.observed: The slider accepted 60. In source mode, cash remaining became 48 CASH while invoice duty was 40 and reserve duty was 10, leaving a 2 CASH backing gap.
actions.taskOutcome: Could vary the amount and compare payment, remaining cash, and duties.
actions.evidence: Slider bounding box 304.55×44px; runtime outputs were 60 CASH, 48 CASH, 40, 10, 50; reached-worksheet.png.

actions.observed: That mode became selected. With the same 60 CASH payment, escrow funding was 112 CASH, cash remaining was 50 CASH, duties totaled 50, and the page said cash matches duties for this one partial. It also says this is a program change, not an S12 action.
actions.taskOutcome: Could compare the source action with the proposed funding policy and see the funding distinction.
actions.evidence: reached-worksheet-proposed.png; selected state from aria-pressed; visible copy says 112 is not an S12 action.

questions.question: Can I switch examples and see which proof roles belong to each one?
questions.answerLocation: Selecting “Batched DEX orders” updates the case description and role cards in the explorer.
questions.remainingClarification: None for the interaction; all examples are described as proposed/illustrative.

questions.question: When I select a role, where do I read what that role means on a phone?
questions.whereItArose: After tapping Pool arithmetic in the mobile role list.
questions.answerLocation: “Inspect an illustrated role” panel after the diagram and role cards.
questions.remainingClarification: The answer is present, but the selected role does not bring the inspector into view; I had to scroll down.

questions.question: Does the slider represent an executed payment, and what changes when I choose full backing?
questions.whereItArose: At the financial worksheet slider and funding-mode buttons.
questions.answerLocation: The worksheet calls itself independent local arithmetic; labels S12 as not executed and the 112 CASH funding as a proposed policy/program change.
questions.remainingClarification: None for this example. It explicitly says later partials need another fee allowance.

questions.question: What does a Web and a Strand mean, and what does this page establish today?
questions.whereItArose: The hero, Explorer, “What is a Strand?” disclosure, and “Current maturity · scoped local evidence” disclosure.
questions.answerLocation: The Strand disclosure says it is an individual proof with its claim, statement, and binding metadata. The maturity disclosure lists bounded local test evidence and says there is no on-chain transaction, and that examples are illustrations.
questions.remainingClarification: The page describes a proposed Web as a handoff from financial requirements through proof roles/Strands to a consuming script; concrete Web integration and settlement remain unestablished.

findings.impact: On a 390×844 screen, selecting a role changes its selected card, but the explanation remains below the diagram and the full role list. The inspector heading begins near the bottom edge, so the tap gives little immediate confirmation about where the details went.
findings.observation: After selecting Pool arithmetic, the inspector heading was at y≈718 in the viewport; I needed a further scroll before the role description was readable.
findings.evidence: reached-role-inspector.png; inspector heading bounding box y=717.67 before scroll.
findings.suggestedChange: On small screens, move the inspector directly after the selected role card or scroll it into view when a role is selected.

findings.impact: The Explore header link is only about 39px wide at this viewport, although it is 44px high.
findings.observation: The small width makes the first header target feel less forgiving than the worksheet and case controls on a touch screen.
findings.evidence: Runtime bounding box for the Explore anchor: 39.05×44px at 390×844; mobile-top.png.
findings.suggestedChange: Give compact header links more horizontal padding on narrow screens.

teachBack: In my words: a Web is the proposed set of required proof roles and the consuming script that should tie financial claims to the concrete step. A Strand is an individual proof carrying a claim, statement, and binding metadata. The page demonstrates a concept and local arithmetic, and it reports bounded local proof-test evidence in its maturity disclosure. It does not establish general Web integration, actual signatures, on-chain proof checking, or settlement. The interactive case diagram and worksheet are explicitly illustrations.
limits: This was a model persona review using an isolated local Chromium browser, not human-user research or a claim to represent disabled users.
I inspected only the assigned frozen HTML, named screenshots, and required Moriarty workflow instructions.
The browser made only the local file request; external HTTP and HTTPS navigation was blocked.
I assessed mobile navigation and clarity, not cryptographic correctness, security, or ledger behavior.
